# spec/run/run

`spec/run` — running an emitted test against a nish install, and reading
its transcript back in the contract's terms: which requirement each
`PASS` / `FAIL` line speaks to, and whether the transcript is the one the
test's own `main` wrote.

Generated from [src/spec/run/run.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/run/run.ts).

A clause's outcome, ordered from best to worst: a requirement takes its clauses' worst.


### runParse

Reads a test's output: each clause's outcome from the line that reports
it (`PASS  [id] …`, `FAIL  [id] …` with its reason indented on the next
line, `SKIP  [id] …`). A line naming no clause of the contract is ignored;
a clause no line names is not-run. A skip of a vector the contract marks
slow, with the slow reason, is marked slow: left out on purpose.

```ts
function runParse(c: Contract, stdout: string): RunClause[]
```

<scalar-field name="c" type="Contract" required>

the contract

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="stdout" type="string" required>

the test's standard output

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="RunClause[]">

one entry per clause, in contract order

</scalar-field>

### runTranscript

Checks that a transcript is the one the emitted test wrote. The module
under test runs in the same process and can print anything, so a clause
line alone proves nothing: the run must reach the end of `main` (its
`vector-done <nonce> <bits>` line, with the nonce this run passed in), every
clause must be reported once and before that line, and each printed outcome
must match what the clause returned to `main` (pass and skip return true).

```ts
function runTranscript(
  c: Contract,
  stdout: string,
  nonce: string,
  clauses: RunClause[],
): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="c" type="Contract" required>

the contract

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="stdout" type="string" required>

the test's standard output

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nonce" type="string" required>

the nonce the run passed the test

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="clauses" type="RunClause[]" required>

the clauses as runParse read them

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

each reason the transcript cannot be trusted; empty when it can

</scalar-field>

### runJudge

Judges a run. Each requirement takes the worst outcome of the clauses that
cover it (not-run when none does), leaving out a slow vector skipped for
want of `--slow`: one covered only by those is a skip. The run is an ERROR
when its transcript cannot be trusted; else VIOLATED when a clause failed;
else an ERROR when a clause other than a slow skip did not pass, every
clause was a slow skip, or the test exited nonzero; else SATISFIED, over what ran.

```ts
function runJudge(
  c: Contract,
  clauses: RunClause[],
  exitCode: i32,
  integrity: string[],
): RunVerdict
```

<scalar-field name="c" type="Contract" required>

the contract

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="clauses" type="RunClause[]" required>

the clauses as runParse read them

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="exitCode" type="i32" required>

the test's exit status

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="integrity" type="string[]" required>

the problems runTranscript found

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="RunVerdict">

the verdict

</scalar-field>

### runNonce

A fresh nonce for one run: 16 random bytes as hex. It is passed to the
test on the command line, never written into its source, so the build
stays cacheable.

```ts
function runNonce(): string
```

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

32 lowercase hex digits

</scalar-field>

### runMakeScratch

Makes a scratch nish install: a copy of the root's seed (runSeedOf)
without its std, the root's own `std/`, and the overrides written over it.
`nish run` resolves `nish/…` imports to the std beside its binary, so a
test run with the scratch's compiler sees the overridden library and
nothing else does. An override reached through a symlink in `std/` is
refused; a link on the overridden file itself is replaced, never written
through, and every other link is left as it is.

```ts
function runMakeScratch(
  nishRoot: string,
  paths: string[],
  texts: string[],
): Result<RunScratch, string>
```

<scalar-field name="nishRoot" type="string" required>

a nish install or checkout

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="paths" type="string[]" required>

where each override goes, relative and under `std/`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="texts" type="string[]" required>

each override's contents, matching `paths`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;RunScratch, string&gt;">

the install, or `Err` when it could not be made (nothing is left behind)

</scalar-field>

### runNishArgv

The command that builds and runs a Nish test: `nish run <file>`, or, when
slow vectors run, `nish run --profile speed <file>`. An optimized build
costs about a second more to compile, and runs a long iterated vector some
ten times faster, so only a run with `--slow` pays for it.

```ts
function runNishArgv(nishBin: string, file: string, slow: boolean): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="nishBin" type="string" required>

the compiler

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="file" type="string" required>

the test

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="slow" type="boolean" required>

whether the test runs its slow vectors

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

the command, without the nonce

</scalar-field>

### runEscape

A line the module printed, made safe to show in a terminal or in markdown:
a control character (an ANSI escape's ESC among them) becomes `\xNN`, a
backtick becomes `'`, and past RUN_LINE_CHARS bytes it is cut, between
characters, with `…`.

```ts
function runEscape(text: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the line

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the line as a report shows it

</scalar-field>

### runFormatText

A run's result as text: the verdict, each requirement's outcome, each slow
vector skipped, each failed clause with its reason, and why the transcript
cannot be trusted.
An ERROR with no clause run shows the end of the compiler's output.

```ts
function runFormatText(r: RunResult): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="r" type="RunResult" required>

the result

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

the report, one line per entry

</scalar-field>

### runFormatMarkdown

A run's result as a markdown section for a PR comment: the verdict, then a
table of the requirements and their outcomes, then each slow vector
skipped, then each failure. What the
module printed goes only inside code spans, escaped by runEscape (which
leaves no backtick), so it cannot add links, HTML or table cells.

```ts
function runFormatMarkdown(r: RunResult): string
```

<scalar-field name="r" type="RunResult" required>

the result

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the markdown

</scalar-field>

### runFormatJson

A run's result as JSON: `{contract, status, exit, requirements: {id:
outcome}, clauses: [{id, outcome, detail}], integrity: [...]}`. A slow
vector skipped for want of `--slow` also has `"slow": true`, and a vector
held to its result's first bytes has `"truncate": {bytes, unit}`.

```ts
function runFormatJson(r: RunResult): string
```

<scalar-field name="r" type="RunResult" required>

the result

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the JSON text, without a trailing newline

</scalar-field>
